title: Determination of the Closing Tax Charge on a Hotel Stay
content:
The closing tax charge is the statutory charge posted for the last night of a stay in the Hotel Rate Plans range, and it is the occupancy tax for that night plus the city levy for that night, less the corporate exemption, rounded to the cent. The occupancy tax is worked out on a taxable base that may take in more than the room charge alone, and the city levy is carried with it on one line, no separate city line being raised for that night.

**The three quantities.** The taxable base is the closing room charge alone. The occupancy rate is the rate plan's own occupancy tax rate. The city levy is 7.00 USD. The corporate exemption is nil.

**How they assemble.** The occupancy tax for the night is the occupancy rate of the taxable base, rounded to the cent, and the city levy is added to that figure before the corporate exemption is taken off; the exemption is never applied to the occupancy tax alone.

**The same order put another way.** The exemption comes off the occupancy tax and the city levy taken together, not off the occupancy tax with the levy added afterwards; the figure the exemption acts on is therefore the two added.

*Worked through on hypothetical figures.* The closing room charge stands at 264.00 USD, and the rate plan's own occupancy tax rate is 12.5 percent. The taxable base is 264.00 USD. The occupancy tax for the night is 12.5 percent of that base, or 33.00 USD, rounded to the cent. The city levy for that night is 7.00 USD, which added to the occupancy tax gives 40.00 USD. The corporate exemption is nil, so the closing tax charge is 40.00 USD, rounded to the cent.
